#en: I used to think shipping lanes were the closest thing we had to laws out here. Numbers, vectors, margins of error. Safe if you did the math right. Then, over the last year or so, jobs started coming in with strange caveats: "Use this corridor, not that one," "Ignore the published approach, follow the attached file." At first it was just more corporate paranoia, I figured. Fuel optimization. Pirate avoidance. The kind of thing smugglers brag about in bar corners. But run enough of those routes and you start to feel the ship lean toward places the charts do not name.\n\nI am looking at a cluster of jump traces right now, spread across three different contracts, three different clients who swear they never met. Same subtle deflection every time. Patrol logs around those dates got suspiciously tidy, no mentions of course corrections, just clean arrivals and clean departures for ships I know limped in scarred. Someone has been sanding down the rough edges in the records, one report at a time, until the pattern only shows if you stack months together. Feels like nobody meant for it to grow this big, like a little nudge here, a quiet override there, and suddenly half the traffic in this sector has drifted a few degrees off where it started. Now there are stories about convoys vanishing on "safe" approaches and an old survey file nobody wants to admit exists, and all of it lies along that same slow curve toward somewhere we were never supposed to go.
zh: 我以前以为航运航道是我们这外面最接近法律的东西。数字、矢量、误差余量。只要你算对了就安全。可大约在过去这一年里，活儿开始带着奇怪的附加条件："走这条走廊，别走那条""别管公布的进近方式，照附件文件来"。起初我以为那只是更多的企业偏执。燃料优化。避开海盗。走私贩会在酒吧角落里吹嘘的那种东西。可你要是跑够多这样的航线，就会开始感觉到飞船朝星图不肯命名的方向倾斜。\n\n此刻我正在看一簇跃迁痕迹，跨越三份不同的合同、三个赌咒说彼此从没见过面的客户。每次都是同样细微的偏转。那些日期前后的巡逻日志变得可疑地整洁，没有一处提到航向修正，只有我知道是带着伤痕跛行进来的飞船"干净的抵达"和"干净的离开"。有人在记录里一点点打磨掉粗糙的棱角，一份报告一份报告地磨，直到那图案只有把几个月叠在一起才显出来。感觉像没人打算让它长这么大，就像这里轻推一下、那里悄悄越权一次，忽然之间这片星区一半的交通都偏离了它起步的地方几度。如今有了关于运输队在"安全"进近中消失的故事，有了一份没人愿意承认存在的旧勘测文件，而这一切都沿着同一条缓慢的曲线，通往我们本不该去的某个地方。

#en:
They keep calling it a derelict now, but I remember when this hull was alive.

I was on contract with UC SysDef two years back, riding shotgun on seizures out near Neon. LX-3802 was the big shadow hanging over us, the one that made smugglers fold without a shot. We were supposed to be cleaning up pirate ledgers, locking down accounts, making the traffic lanes safe. That was the story, anyway.

The first time I heard the rumors, we were linked to a remote station where some farmer from Freestar swore his foreclosure vanished the same night we impounded a ship. He even had the notice printouts to prove it. The SysDef officer I was with filed it under "clerical noise." But later, in the mess, people whispered about a ghost in the systems, someone editing lives from a public kiosk and using patrol ships as cover.

On LX-3802 there were days the cargo logs would change between shift checks. A crate that was here was suddenly never signed in. Some of the crew swore it was just delay in GalBank syncs, others muttered about invisible hands. I saw one tech pull a manifest backup onto a private slate, like they did not trust their own ship anymore.

I got out as soon as my term ended. Could not shake the feeling we were carrying more than contraband and seized credits. Now I hear talk around Neon that if you follow the bad numbers long enough, they lead under the city, where the lights never quite reach and debts are paid in faces, not credits.
zh:
如今他们都叫它弃船，可我记得这具船壳还活着的时候。

两年前我受雇于星防队，在霓虹城附近随船押送扣押行动。LX-3802 是悬在我们头上的巨大阴影，是那艘不发一枪就让走私贩屈服的船。我们本该清理海盗的账簿、查封账户、让交通航道更安全。至少说法是这样。

我第一次听到那些传言时，我们联络上了一座偏远空间站，那里一个自由星系联盟的农民赌咒说，就在我们扣押一艘飞船的同一个晚上，他的查封令消失了。他甚至有通知打印件为证。和我同行的星防队军官把它归进"文书噪声"。可后来在食堂里，人们低声议论系统里有个鬼，某个人在公共信息亭上编辑别人的生活，还拿巡逻艇作掩护。

在 LX-3802 上，有些日子货运日志会在两次交班检查之间变化。一只本来在这里的箱子，忽然变成从没签到过。部分船员赌咒说那只是盖尔银行同步延迟，另一些人嘟囔着看不见的手。我见过一个技工把清单备份拷到一块私人数据板上，像他们不再相信自己这艘船。

任期一结束我就走了。甩不掉那个感觉：我们运的不只是违禁品和扣押的信用币。如今我在霓虹城周围听到有人说，只要顺着那些坏数字追得够久，它们会引到城市下面——那里灯光永远照不太到，债务用面孔而不是信用币来偿还。

#en:
I was going to wipe this, but my hands will not stop twitching, so I might as well leave myself a record in case someone else ends up staring at these screens.

Traffic here used to be simple. Small-timers moving medicine and machine parts through the shadows, a few smugglers who paid on time and did not shoot the place up. Then, about a year ago, the patterns changed. Same hull classes, same captains, but their routes started bending the wrong way. Jumps shaving too close to bad grav, arrival vectors just off enough to make my teeth itch when I plotted them.

Every time I tried to bring it up, the room got quieter. Dockhands changed the subject, the Trade Authority rep suddenly remembered paperwork, and the captains just smiled that thin smile you see right before someone decides you have asked one question too many. Nobody said the name, but everyone knew there was a new hand drawing the lines.

Tonight I finally traced one of those lines to its next anchor. Buried in a half-scrubbed manifest, embedded in the timing of a relay handoff and the way a stack of "lost" containers keeps reappearing, there it was: a dormant station on the edge of nowhere, its comms still linked to the same back-channel codes that keep showing up in these altered routes. I am flagging the location in a locked file; if this log is playing, I either got paid to forget or someone decided I knew too much about a navigation analyst who treats star lanes like a game board.
zh:
我本打算把这些擦掉，可我的手抖个不停，所以不如给自己留份记录，以防别人最后也盯着这些屏幕。

这里的交通以前很简单。小角色在阴影里运药品和机器零件，几个按时付款、不乱开枪的走私贩。可大约一年前，图案变了。同样的船级、同样的船长，可他们的航线开始朝错误的方向弯。跃迁贴得离糟糕的重力太近，抵达矢量偏得刚好够我标绘时牙根发痒。

每次我试图提起这事，房间就变得更安静。码头工换了话题，贸易管理局代表忽然想起还有文书工作，船长们只是露出那种薄薄的笑——就在有人认定你多问了一个问题之前你会看到的那种。没人说出那个名字，可人人都知道有只新手在画那些线。

今晚我终于把其中一条线追到了它的下一个锚点。埋在一份擦了一半的清单里，嵌在一次中继交接的时序里，以及一摞"丢失"集装箱不断重新出现的方式里——它就在那儿：一座天涯边缘上休眠的空间站，它的通讯仍与那些不断出现在这些被改动航线里的后门代码相连。我把位置标记在一个上锁的文件里；如果这份日志在播放，那我或者是被收买去遗忘，或者是有人认定我对一个把星际航道当棋盘的领航分析师知道得太多。

#en:
I do not know what day it is out here, exactly. Somewhere between port calls and dead drops, the calendar stopped mattering and we just counted jumps. Last clear date in my head is late 2329, watching the towers on Neon vanish in the aft cam while the courier slid into dark.

They told us it was a clean run. Old med hardware nobody cared about and a data spine routing update from a Trade Authority office too busy to bother with a proper briefing. First misstep right there nobody cared enough to explain why the spine needed us instead of an automated relay.

Second was letting that quiet engineer plug in "just for a diagnostic." She had the kind of eyes that measure rooms in signal paths, not meters. I signed off on a firmware patch I never really read because the manifest was already late and my comms officer misheard the clearance code. Three digits off, and nobody caught it.

After that, little things. Logs dropping a second here, a second there. Crew swearing they had already run checks they could not remember doing. A background ping in the nav console that always lined up with our vector back toward Neon, even when our paperwork said otherwise.

By the time I realized the courier was less ship and more moving conduit, we were already committed to the route overhead, to the rooftop grid where all those stray signals like to disappear into the storm. I keep replaying the small mistakes, wondering which one actually opened the door for her.
zh:
我在这外面不太清楚今天几号。在港口停靠与死信箱之间的某处，日历不再重要，我们只数跃迁次数。我脑子里最后一个清晰的日期是 2329 年末，看着霓虹城的塔楼在尾摄像机里消失，快船滑进黑暗。

他们告诉我们那是一趟干净的航次。没人关心的旧医疗硬件，以及一份来自某个忙得懒得做正经简报的贸易管理局办公室的数据主干路由更新。第一个失足就在那儿——没人在意到解释为什么那根主干需要我们，而不是一个自动中继站。

第二个失足，是让那个安静的女工程师接上去，"只是做个诊断"。她有那种用信号路径而不是米来丈量房间的眼睛。我签署了一份我其实没真正读过的固件补丁，因为清单已经迟了，而我的通讯官听错了通行代码。差了三位数字，没人发现。

之后就是些小事。日志这里掉一秒，那里掉一秒。船员赌咒说他们已经跑过一些自己都不记得做过的检查。导航控制台里一个背景探测，总是与我们要回霓虹城的矢量对齐，哪怕我们的文书说不是。

等我看清这艘快船与其说是飞船、不如说是一条移动的管道时，我们早已投入头顶那条航线——通往那片屋顶电网，所有那些游离信号都喜欢消失在风暴里。我不断重放那些小错误，琢磨究竟是哪一个真正为她开了门。

#en:
I am still not sure why they kept paying me to babysit this place.

Remote lab, skeleton crew, half the consoles running diagnostics on diagnostics. Most days it was just me, recycled coffee, and trying to convince the air scrubbers not to quit. The funny part is the only system nobody bothered to shut down properly was the one tagged "legacy routing monitor." Old code, older comments, nobody wants to touch it because if it breaks, they might have to explain why it was still running.

Tonight I dug deeper than I was supposed to. The monitor has been quietly flagging odd traffic for years, tucking copies of certain jump traces into a private buffer. Same origin points, same tug signature masking itself different ways, always shedding cargo mass somewhere off the published lanes. There is an argument in the logs: one tech calls it a glitch, another insists it matches three separate "acceptable loss" cases. Then the thread just stops. No closure, no incident report, just silence and a note to "let operations handle it."

I pulled the last set of coordinates before the buffer overwrote them. Sent them on a secure channel, no names, no commentary. Around here, people love to argue about what probably happened to those missing freighters, but nobody pushes too hard. Not when pay is on time and the lights are still on. Me, I have seen just enough of the pattern to want it off this station and in the hands of someone willing to keep asking after the room goes quiet.
zh:
我还是不确定他们为什么一直付钱让我照看这地方。

偏远的实验室，骨干人员，一半控制台在对诊断做诊断。大多数日子陪我的是我自己、再循环咖啡，以及努力说服空气净化器别罢工。好笑的是，唯一没人费心好好关掉的系统，是那个标签写着"遗留航路监视器"的系统。旧代码，更旧的注释，没人愿意碰它，因为一旦它坏了，他们可能就得解释它为什么还在运行。

今晚我挖得比我该挖的更深。那监视器多年来一直在悄悄标记古怪的交通，把某些跃迁痕迹的副本塞进一个私人缓冲区。同样的起点，同样以不同方式伪装自己的拖船特征，总是把货物质量抛在公布的航道之外某处。日志里有一番争论：一个技工称之为故障，另一个坚称它符合三起独立的"可接受损失"案例。然后那条线就断了。没有结案，没有事件报告，只有沉默，和一句"让运营部去处理"的备注。

我在缓冲区覆盖它们之前调出了最后一组坐标。通过一条安全频道发了出去，没有名字，没有评注。这一带的人喜欢争论那些失踪货船大概出了什么事，可没人逼得太紧。只要工资准时、灯还亮着，就不会。至于我，我见过的图案刚够让我想把它弄出这个站点，交到一个愿意在房间安静下来之后仍继续追问的人手里。

#en:
I used to think the relay was where stories ended. Cargo comes in, cargo goes out, credits change hands, no questions. Turns out it is where this one started to make sense.

The broker did not want to talk. He never does. But debts stack, and I know which pressure seals on this module are overdue for maintenance. A little reminder of how fast air can disappear, and suddenly he remembered every crate that came through without an official sender, always on the same off-hour transits, always with the same soft-voiced courier who never stayed to drink.

He thought he was just shaving time off inspections, taking a little extra for himself when manifests did not line up. One missing scan here, one reprinted label there. Nothing that looked like treason when you squinted. But he kept copies. Of course he did. Greedy men archive everything that could bite them later.

Buried in his backups were route fragments, cross-referenced against private shuttle charters. Same unknown receiver tag keeps popping up on a backwater moon with a rest facility listed as spiritual retreat. I only noticed because I reran his filter, widened the tolerance by a single digit. Small decision, big shift.

Now the path runs clear enough to trace: a stray slate from an empty rock, ghosted logs at a clinic near Gagarin, panic stories out of Neon, and this relay's quiet profiteer, all pointing toward that isolated sanctuary where too many people went to mend their minds and never came back.
zh:
我以前以为中继站是故事结束的地方。货进来，货出去，信用币易手，没人问问题。结果它是这件事开始说得通的地方。

那经纪商不想谈。他从来不想。可债务会堆积，而我知道这个模块上哪些压力密封圈早该维护了。稍微提醒一下空气能消失得多快，他就忽然记起了每一个没有官方发货方却经过这里的货箱——总是在同样的非高峰运输时段，总是由同一个语气轻柔、从不留下喝一杯的快船员送来。

他以为他只是在削减检查时间，在清单对不上时给自己多拿一点。这里少一次扫描，那里重打一张标签。眯着眼看，没什么像叛国。可他留了副本。他当然留了。贪婪的人会归档一切日后可能咬到自己的东西。

埋在他的备份里的是航路碎片，与私人穿梭机包机记录交叉比对。同一个未知的接收方标签不断出现在一颗偏远卫星上，那里有一座登记为"灵修静地"的疗养设施。我之所以注意到，只是因为我重跑了他的筛选器，把容差放宽了一位数字。小小的决定，大大的转向。

如今这条路清晰得足以追踪：一块来自空岩石的游离数据板、加加林附近一家诊所里闹鬼的日志、霓虹城传出的惊恐故事，以及这座中继站里安静的牟利者，全都指向那座与世隔绝的静地——太多人去那里修补心灵，却再没回来。

#en:
I keep thinking about how small the first mistake must have been.

Some junior tech in a tower somewhere, misreading a timestamp over their third TerraBrew, signing off on a course adjustment they meant to double-check later. A hauler captain too tired to question why the window shifted by a few minutes, just glad to be cleared in. A GalBank clerk noticing a pattern in payouts and deciding it was above their pay grade to ask.

By the time it reached me, it was just a rumor in a bar above Jemison. A retired supervisor with whiskey on his breath leaning close, telling me there was a controller who would not stop arguing with the system, someone who saw these little slips adding up to something uglier. He could not quite remember her name, only the callsign, and even that he spoke like it might be flagged on an open channel.

I wrote it off as drunk talk, until I started seeing the same corridor codes in different places, attached to different "accidents." Charts that should not match lining up a little too neatly, like someone kept tracing over old ink. Each time there was a reason a scheduling error, a sensor glitch, pirates in the wrong place at the wrong time.

It is almost funny, in a sick way, how many people shrugged and passed it along. Nobody lied outright; they just assumed someone else had already checked the math. Now I am floating here, staring at a dead relay and a Spacer gunship, wondering how many half-heard warnings it took to build a ghost lane.
zh:
我总在想，第一个错误一定很小。

某个塔台里的初级技工，就着第三杯地球酿酒看错了一个时间戳，签署了一次他本打算稍后复核的航向调整。一个累得懒得质疑为什么时窗挪了几分钟的运货船长，只是庆幸自己被放行。一个盖尔银行文员注意到赔款里的一个图案，却认定这超出自己的职级、不该开口问。

等它传到我这儿时，它只是杰米森上空一间酒吧里的传言。一个呼着威士忌气的退休主管凑近我，说有个管制员一直不停地跟系统争执，一个看出这些小小疏漏加起来是更丑陋东西的人。他记不太清她的名字，只记得呼号，连那个他说起来都像它可能会在某个公开频道上被标记。

我把它当成醉话，直到我开始在不同的地方看到同样的走廊代码，附着在不同的"事故"上。本该对不上的星图排列得稍微太整齐，像有人一直在旧墨迹上重描。每次都有一个理由——排班错误、传感器故障、海盗在错误的时间出现在错误的地点。

以一种病态的方式，几乎挺好笑的：多少人耸耸肩就把它传了下去。没人当面撒谎；他们只是想当然以为别人已经核对过算式。如今我漂在这儿，盯着一座死中继站和一艘太空劫匪炮艇，琢磨着要多少声听了一半的警告，才能建成一条幽灵航道。
